attempted_axis: Reopen-triage drive of the 2026-08-29 park against the September law wave: re-measured first, found the residual had collapsed to THREE clusters in a 1598-instruction function with an IDENTICAL opcode multiset, and closed two of the three at once with a staging local that fixes call-argument emission order.

attributes.law_screen: claim.law.declaration-order-numbers-the-registers-assignment-order-schedules-the-loads.20260901.v1 APPLIED and is the whole win - it post-dates the 2026-08-29 park, and the park's residual line already named the cluster ('SetSkinFX arg eval order lwz-first vs lfs-first') without a lever for it. claim.law.extern-scalar-read-defeats-fp-literal-hoist.20260831.v1 APPLIED FIRST and measured NEGATIVE, byte-identical: respelling the `1.0f` argument as the already-declared `extern f32 lbl_80347790` (the TU spells it that way at :5539) did not defeat the hoist. The reason is a genuine BOUNDARY on that law and is recorded separately as claim.law.RC_extern-fp-symbol-cannot-defeat-a-hoist-when-the-extern-IS-the-pool-entry.20260901.v1: the literal and the extern read compile to the IDENTICAL `lfs f1,@SDA21` instruction, so the provenance distinction is erased before scheduling and the law has nothing to bite on. claim.law.explicit-fp-symbol-vs-literal-zero-regression.20260830.v1 APPLIED as a VETO on the one remaining lever, and its precondition holds exactly: it names this codebase's convention of a canonical sdata2 zero extern that is ALSO reachable as a plain literal, its provenance is pmotion.c::PlayerMotion in this same project, and it measured a whole-function cascade (insns +1, real 3782 -> 4149) from exactly the substitution the last cluster invites. It further warns that the target ALSO uses anonymous-looking pool constants at such sites and that reading fnasm's resolved symbol name as proof the target spelled a SYMBOL is the specific misreading to avoid - which is what my `lbl_80347750`/`lbl_803477AC` vs `@@124`/`@@310` observation would otherwise have been. The symbolify probe was therefore NOT spent. claim.law.pool-literal-substitution-is-per-function.20260831.v1 reinforces the veto: of 48 functions a driver wanted to keep from such a sweep, only 2 survived second-stage validation. attempt.mbdrawblits-hoisted-constant-deal-order-permutation.20260901.v1 SCREENED as the matching mechanism record for the surviving cluster; its statement-reorder axis is already recorded dead, so it was not re-run. claim.law.adding-a-local-renumbers-the-anonymous-pool-and-drifts-siblings.20260831.v1 SCREENED as the hazard of the cure (two locals added) and measured CLEAR - the TU gate reports no sibling movement. claim.law.webfrank-pinned-function-source-freeze.20260831.v1 SCREENED: game/game/player pins ExpToLevel, do_heal_players and load_player_geo, none of them this function.
attributes.residual: IMPROVED and retained: real 392 -> 384, fuzzy 98.598 -> 99.0989, insns 1598/1598 with opcode multiset IDENTICAL throughout. TWO of the three clusters are CLOSED. What closed them: clusters at +0x678 and +0x6d0 were the SAME residual at two sites - the two SetSkinFX calls in the shield-flag arms (src/game/game/player.c:5150-5162). Target emits the argument setup as `lwz r4,<global>` then `addi r3,r31,2012` then `lfs f1,<1.0f pool>`; ours emitted exactly the reverse, `lfs f1` then `addi r3` then `lwz r4`, i.e. left-to-right source order against target's right-to-left. Note the registers CANNOT discriminate the parameter order here (r3=v, r4=color, f1=scale hold regardless of how the prototype is permuted, because GPR and FPR argument slots are assigned independently), so only the EMISSION order carries the signal. CURE, one line per site: stage the extern read into a local immediately before the call - `s32 skin = lbl_80344BF0; SetSkinFX(1.0f, (f32*)((u8*)p + 0x7DC), skin, 1, 1);` - which forces the `lwz` to be emitted as its own statement ahead of the call and reproduces the target's order at BOTH sites simultaneously. This is a direct application of claim.law.declaration-order-numbers-the-registers-assignment-order-schedules-the-loads.20260901.v1, a law that POST-DATES the park, which is why the park could not have screened it. WHAT REMAINS, one cluster, named to the instruction: at +0x1ac, five loop-invariant pool constants are dealt into the same five slots in a different ORDER. Target deals lbl_80347750(f64), lbl_803477AC(f32), lbl_803477D0(f64), lbl_803477D8(f32), lbl_80347A40(f64) - strictly ASCENDING pool address. Ours deals 803477D0, 803477D8, 80347A40 first (the three spelled as extern symbols in the locals at player.c:5010-5012, in source-statement order) and then the two that our source spells as plain literals - the f64 `0.0` at :5019 and the f32 `0.0f` at :5033. This is precisely the mechanism recorded in attempt.mbdrawblits-hoisted-constant-deal-order-permutation.20260901.v1 (target deals in ascending pool address, ours in source statement order), and MBDrawBlits already KILLED the statement-reorder axis there.
